source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Allow each unit to define infection events independently so local clinical judgment can replace standardized surveillance criteria.","B":"Increase the raw number of reported infections by using broader definitions, regardless of whether comparisons remain clinically meaningful.","C":"Create consistent case identification across settings so rates can be compared, benchmarked, and followed reliably over time in practice.","D":"Limit surveillance to research hospitals because standardized definitions are not intended for routine infection-prevention programs."}}
source_row.rationale: Standardized surveillance definitions (such as those from the CDC's National Healthcare Safety Network) ensure that infections like CLABSI are identified and counted consistently across different units and facilities, supporting accurate, comparable data collection essential for meaningful benchmarking, trend identification, and quality improvement efforts.
source_row.source_detail: CDC NHSN 2026 Patient Safety Component, Bloodstream Infection Event protocol: standardized definitions and criteria for identifying CLABSI and related laboratory-confirmed bloodstream infection events. 2026 NHSN protocol/current page reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: CDC NHSN — Standardized Surveillance Definitions for Healthcare-Associated Infections
source_row.stem: A hospital's infection prevention team tracks central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) using standardized surveillance definitions, and a unit manager assumes each unit could reasonably just use its own criteria for what counts as this kind of infection.
